corrections.before:
READI randomly offered intensive employment, cognitive-behavioral programming and support. Only 55% began programming. Its 12% lower victimization estimate is treatment-on-the-treated relative to control compliers, not a significant intent-to-treat reduction or a UPI coefficient. The primary violence index was not significantly improved; outreach-referred participants had a stronger 43% victimization estimate. The 11 events per 100 controls over 20 months is a rate benchmark, not the same estimation denominator. I retain r=.04 and e=.10 as uncertain transport judgments for heterogeneous UPI-supported services, not study-derived effects. [Original trial](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10898100/)

A closer local study models nonrandomized GRYD incident response in 2014–17, using spatial-temporally sampled controls. It estimates roughly 14–18% lower retaliatory triggering, with meaningful model and inferential uncertainty. This is neither all violence nor the incremental effect of UPI, training, or Peacemakers. Existing GRYD is part of the baseline; the study supports mechanism plausibility without supporting direct transplantation of a headline reduction. [Original local study](https://www.pjeffreybrantingham.com/_files/ugd/50eba0_8b88fa1624d442979bbff5c880935271.pdf)

Mortality value is now an explicit finite survival calculation: .8 health utility, a 47-year cap, 1% annual all-cause mortality and 3% discounting produce 16.7227 QALYs per initially avoided death. The mortality hazard and cap are judgments, not a recipient life table; future victimization risk has not disappeared. Nonfatal value is .1 acute QALY plus .05 annual utility loss for at most ten years, with the same survival/discounting, totaling .5047 QALY. The small Boston cohort supports ongoing morbidity but does not estimate these parameters. Fatal and nonfatal branches are mutually exclusive. [Survivor study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32530586/)

Only one service year is central. Extra downstream health is not another program year. Continued exposure to violence, displacement to other people or neighborhoods, worker injury/burnout and privacy harms can erode or reverse benefit. No arrest, crime-cost dollar or reported mediation is directly converted to QALYs. The Richmond evidence previously reviewed remains contextual, not an additional credited channel.

corrections.before:
FY2025 revenue was $12,539,904, government grants $5,292,475, cash $6,898,638, unrestricted net assets $6,213,733 and total liabilities $2,716,158. Cash equals about 9.3 months of FY2025 expense before commitments; that is not a current runway. The balance includes restrictions and obligations, and the correct FY2025 audit is still needed. FY2024 audited notes document concentrated funding and accrued external grants, illustrating why gross cash is not a spendable gap. [Latest accounts](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202630969349301208/IRS990)

UPI announced an $8 million Ballmer commitment over two years in July 2024 and says Peacemakers funding ends in 2026. This is historical committed support, not a fresh 2026 renewal or an extra amount to add to annual revenue. No verified remaining Peacemakers gap, renewal probability or marginal hiring budget was found. [Ballmer announcement](https://www.urbanpeaceinstitute.org/2024-7-17-upi-receives-8m-grant-from-ballmer-group/) [Dated cliff claim](https://www.urbanpeaceinstitute.org/homicides-drop-by-nearly-27-in-neighborhoods-most-impacted-by-violence-in-2025/)

The cliff is not all-recipient shutdown: BSCC identifies a separate UPI frontline-training contract from August 2025 through June 2029. Los Angeles also approved a $5.087 million Safe Passage award, with $3,438,380 in provider contracts including Community Partners and Alliance for Community Empowerment, recipient routes also appearing in UPI grants. Council authorization and appropriation do not by themselves prove every contract has been executed or replaces identical services. They do establish a material funded baseline to investigate, not zero public support. [BSCC](https://www.bscc.ca.gov/s_cpgpcalvipgrant/) [Named allocation](https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2026/26-0542_rpt_cao_05-27-26.pdf) [Adopted recommendations](https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2026/26-0542_rpt_ps_bf_06-16-26.pdf) [Final appropriation](https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2026/26-0542_CAF_8-13-26.pdf)

Central b=.5 remains an explicitly subjective effective capacity response to ordinary private support after reserves, replacement donors, secured grants and current commitments; a=.75 separately represents the UPI-enabled share of service benefit. These discounts must not be estimated from the same loss twice. A short-bridge case credits only a quarter-year gap and then assumes other funding resumes. Complete replacement produces zero. UPI itself describes trust and information-sharing concerns with federal funding; the report treats these as documented organizational constraints, not an independent legal finding. [UPI statement](https://www.urbanpeaceinstitute.org/concerns-regarding-recent-changes-to-doj-cvipi-funding/)

The filing labeled FY2025 contains FY2024 statements plus a February 2026 corrective-action attachment about recurring contribution-recognition controls. The period mismatch remains unresolved; obtain the correctly matched audit, implementation evidence and a current unrestricted cash/commitments schedule before treating this as donor-ready.
